title: Securities Dealing Policy (Version 4.0)
date_approved: 17 August 2023 (BSP Board; Board Audit & Compliance Committee 16 August 2023)
date_next_review: Every 2 years, or earlier if required

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: All directors and officers of BSP including the Group CEO and the Company Secretary; all directors and company secretaries of BSP Group; all members of BSP's Executive Committee; all General Managers, their executive assistants and Deputy General Managers; all Country Managers and Country Heads; all Business Unit Heads; all Finance & Planning staff involved with preparation of financial records; all employees with knowledge of financial performance or operational information not known to the market; all Independent Committee Members; and any BSP Employee designated by the Board. Must not deal in Company Securities without prior approval and outside a Trading Window, and is subject to the absolute hedging ban, the short-term and speculative trading ban and the secured financing approval gate.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The chairman of the Board of BSP. Distinguished only for approvals: consent, approval and waivers come from the Chairperson of BSP's Board Audit and Compliance Committee (or delegate), with a copy to the Company Secretary. The Chairman is also the approver for margin lending and other secured financing arrangements by any Restricted Person under clause 3.8.3.

tiers.name: All directors of BSP (except the Chairman)
tiers.description: Directors of BSP other than the Chairman. Consent, approval and waivers come from the Chairman (or delegate), with a copy to the Company Secretary. After dealing they must give the Company Secretary the price and quantity of securities traded so BSP can notify PNGX, ASX and SPX of the change in the director's interests.

tiers.name: All chairpersons of BSP Group
tiers.description: Chairpersons of the boards of BSP Group subsidiaries. Consent, approval and waivers come from the Chairperson of the respective subsidiary's Board Audit and Compliance Committee (or delegate), with copies to the Company Secretary and the subsidiary's company secretary.

tiers.name: All directors of BSP Group (except the chairpersons)
tiers.description: Directors of BSP Group subsidiaries other than the chairpersons. Consent, approval and waivers come from the chairperson of the respective subsidiary board (or delegate), with copies to the Company Secretary and the subsidiary's company secretary.

tiers.name: Independent Committee Members
tiers.description: Independent members of board committees. Consent, approval and waivers come from the chairperson of the respective board committee (or delegate), with copies to the Company Secretary and the respective board's company secretary.

tiers.name: All other Restricted Persons not specified above
tiers.description: Executive Committee members, General Managers and their executive assistants, Deputy General Managers, Country Managers and Heads, Business Unit Heads, Finance & Planning staff and other designated employees. Consent, approval and waivers come from the CEO (or delegate), with a copy to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Closely Connected Person
tiers.description: A Close Family Member (spouse or de facto, any children whether minor or adult, or parent of or living with the Restricted Person, including children of the spouse or de facto) or a Closely Connected Entity (any family company or family trust that the Restricted Person or their close family members may control or have an interest in). Each Restricted Person must ensure dealings by their Closely Connected Persons comply with the Policy and that those persons are aware of it.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board controls the windows directly. A Trading Window is opened only by a decision of the Board in consultation with the Company Secretary, and once opened the Company Secretary notifies Restricted Persons by email or intranet and notifies the share registries and brokers. 'A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board at any time', and 'Restricted Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant results announcement.' The policy does not say whether a suspension or its reason is confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not the subject of a separate rule, but Securities is defined to include 'warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to shares', with no venue limitation, so an exchange-traded or OTC option over BSP shares is a Company Security and dealing in it requires prior approval and must fall in a Trading Window. In practice almost any derivative a director would want is separately caught: hedging transactions are banned outright by 3.8.2 and forward contracts and short sales by 3.8.1.
rules.evidence: Securities: Shares, debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, preference shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to shares

rules.detail: A flat, unqualified ban on hedging exposure to Company Securities. There is no clearance or approval route, no distinction between vested, unvested or locked securities, no distinction between plan and non-plan securities, and no exception in clause 3.6. The only conceivable relief is the clause 3.7 waiver, which is available only where the Restricted Person is selling and not buying, so it cannot authorise the purchase of a put.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.

rules.detail: Forward contracts are expressly named within the ban on short-term and speculative trading, so a prepaid forward or similar monetisation is prohibited on its face, and any such structure is also a transaction designed to hedge exposure to Company Securities contrary to 3.8.2.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling.

rules.detail: Short-selling is named expressly within the ban on short-term and speculative trading, with no approval route and no exception.
rules.evidence: including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. There is no definition of 'deal' or 'dealing' that would sweep a stock loan in, and clause 3.8.3 addresses financing taken by the Restricted Person rather than the lending out of securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative relating to shares and so a Company Security, and it falls within the ban on trading for speculative gain and, where used to reduce exposure, within the outright hedging ban. There is no approval route for either prohibition.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain

rules.detail: Margin lending in respect of Company Securities is permitted with the prior approval of the Chairman (or delegate). Where such approval has been granted, an involuntary disposal resulting from the margin lender exercising its rights is one of the limited dealings permitted outside a Trading Window.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage, lien or pledge is not separately named. Encumbering Company Securities is regulated only as the security component of a margin lending or other secured financing arrangement under 3.8.3, which requires the prior approval of the Chairman or delegate. An encumbrance unconnected with financing is not addressed and is not caught by any dealing definition.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.

rules.detail: The prohibition on 'margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities' is expressly subject to prior Chairman approval, so a bank loan secured on BSP shares is available in principle. Approval sits with the Chairman (or delegate) for every Restricted Person, unlike the clause 3.11 table which routes ordinary dealing approvals elsewhere. No conditions, LVR limits or price triggers are specified.
rules.evidence: unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.

rules.detail: Ban on trading in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, with a defined period: BSP considers short-term to be 6 months or less. On-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling are named. No carve-outs are stated, including none for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling. BSP considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.

exemption_authority: The person specified in the clause 3.11 table may grant a waiver from clauses 3.2 and 3.4 in exceptional circumstances, being severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or court enforceable undertaking, an overriding regulatory requirement, or any other circumstances deemed exceptional. A waiver will only be granted if the application is accompanied by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available and confirmation of no inside information, and only where the Restricted Person is selling and not buying. It may be given or refused without reasons, may be subject to conditions at BSP's absolute discretion, can be withdrawn if new circumstances come to light, lasts 10 Business Days, and refusal is final, binding and must be kept confidential. No waiver power is expressed for the clause 3.8 prohibitions on hedging, short-term and speculative trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not engage in transactions designed to hedge their exposure to Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single sentence defeats a funded collar: the put and call legs are transactions designed to hedge exposure, the ban has no approval or waiver route and no vesting-state carve-out, and it applies to every Restricted Person and their Closely Connected Persons.

bespoke_clauses.topic: financing is approvable but hedging is not
bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, unless the prior approval of the Chairman (or his or her delegate) has been obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is available with Chairman approval, so an unhedged secured loan against BSP shares is possible even though the collar that would normally accompany it is not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities on a short-term basis or for speculative trading gain, including on-market short-term buying and selling, forward contracts and short-selling. BSP considers "short-term" to be a period of 6 months or less.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forward contracts are prohibited by name, closing off prepaid forwards and forward-sale monetisations as an alternative to a collar, and any hedge unwound within 6 months would independently breach the short-term ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A waiver will only be granted if ... the Restricted Person is selling not buying Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the exceptional circumstances route cannot authorise buying a put or entering a derivative position, so there is no discretionary path to a collar; the only sanctioned way to raise cash against a holding is an outright sale or an approved secured loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All periods that are not Trading Windows are "closed periods" for the purposes of the Listing Rules, during which time Restricted Persons are prohibited from dealing in Company Securities. ... A Trading Window may be varied, suspended or withdrawn by the Board at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Dealing is prohibited by default and permitted only inside four announced windows totalling roughly 70 business days a year, and the Board can suspend a window at any moment, so any transaction timetable is fragile.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no assumption of an open window
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons may not assume that a Trading Window is open, even after the relevant results announcement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot infer an open window from the results calendar and must see the Company Secretary's written notification before any leg is executed.

bespoke_clauses.topic: five day notice and five day execution
bespoke_clauses.clause: made in writing to the respective persons specified in clause 3.11 at least 5 Business Days prior to the proposed dealing taking place ... If approved, the confirmation must specify a period of time of no more than 5 Business Days within which the dealing must be completed.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Five business days' advance notice plus a maximum five business day execution window means pricing must be arranged in advance and cannot be left to the moment of approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prior notification, its receipt, any acknowledgement of or response to any such notification is not an endorsement, approval or recommendation of the proposed dealing. Restricted Persons remain responsible for their own investment decisions and compliance with applicable laws and this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Chairman or Company Secretary sign-off gives the bank no comfort, so it must take its own representations on inside information and policy compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: where a Restricted Person has been granted approval to enter into margin lending or other secured financing arrangements (see clause 3.8.3), an involuntary disposal of securities that results from the margin lender or financier exercising its rights under the arrangement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The lender's enforcement sale is permitted outside a Trading Window only if the financing itself was approved in advance, so an unapproved facility leaves the client in breach on enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Each Restricted Person must ensure that: any dealing by their Closely Connected Persons are undertaken in accordance with this Policy ... Closely Connected Entity: Any family company or family trust that the Restricted Person or their close family member(s) may control or have an interest in.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban and financing gate reach family trusts and companies in which the person merely has an interest, so no holding structure escapes them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under the Papua New Guinea Capital Market Act 2015, Australian Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), PNGX Listing Rules, ASX Listing Rules, SPX Listing Rules ... Where this Policy is inconsistent with an applicable law, regulation or prudential standard within a relevant jurisdiction, the Policy applies only to the extent applicable.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: BSP is PNG-incorporated and triple listed, so any structure must clear PNG capital markets law and Bank of PNG prudential standards as well as Australian law, and disclosure runs to three exchanges.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must keep, and make available to the Company Secretary ... on request, a register of dealings by themselves and their Closely Connected Persons, in the form of a record of every dealing, together with supporting material such as contract notes or their equivalent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of any structure must be documented and producible to the Company on demand, so nothing about a financing arrangement can be kept private from BSP.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Clause 3.8.2 bans outright any transaction designed to hedge exposure to Company Securities, with no approval route, no vesting-state carve-out and no exception in clause 3.6, and the clause 3.7 waiver cannot help because it is granted only where the Restricted Person is selling and not buying. Clause 3.8.1 independently prohibits forward contracts, short-selling and any trading on a short-term basis, defined as 6 months or less, which closes off prepaid forwards and other monetisation substitutes. The loan leg on its own is achievable: clause 3.8.3 permits margin lending and other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities with the prior approval of the Chairman or delegate, and clause 3.6.1(e) then treats a financier's enforcement sale as a permitted dealing outside a Trading Window, so an unhedged secured facility over BSP shares is the only viable version of the structure. Any such facility must be documented with 5 Business Days' prior written notice to the approver in the clause 3.11 table, executed within a maximum 5 Business Day approval window that must itself fall inside one of the four announced Trading Windows, notified to the Company Secretary on completion, recorded in the person's own register of dealings, and, for directors, disclosed to PNGX, ASX and SPX.
